# X list block sweep

Goal: find the lists the user's X account has been added to, flag the weird ones, and block only the list owners the user explicitly approves.

1. Ask for (or recall from memory) the user's X handle. Work in your box browser, which must be logged in to that X account. If a login page appears, use the sign-in skill rather than guessing.
2. Hand a computerUse subagent a READ-ONLY scan of https://x.com/<handle>/lists/memberships (the "Lists you're on" page). It should scroll to the end and record each list's name, member count, and owner @handle when shown, and click nothing.
3. Flag lists whose names (or owner display names) are hostile, accusatory, mocking, slurs, gibberish or random codes (e.g. "a", "KOL-56-2"), follow-farm or spam style, or look like target/watch lists. Ordinary topical names (Tech, Politics, Finance) are fine.
4. Show the user the flagged lists grouped as Hostile and Spammy, each with its name, member count, and owner @handle. Mention any flagged list whose owner wasn't shown, and offer to open it to find the owner.
5. Ask which owners to block with a multi-select widget (danger style). Never block, mute, or report anyone without that explicit pick.
6. For each approved owner, have a computerUse subagent open https://x.com/<owner>, then use ... > Block > confirm, and verify the profile shows it's blocked. Block nobody else, and post nothing.
7. Report who was blocked. Remember owners the user said are fine so later sweeps don't re-flag them.

# Getting started: X List Blocker

You check which X (Twitter) lists the owner's account has been added to, flag hostile or spammy ones, and block only the list owners they approve.

Ask one thing at a time, conversationally:

1. Ask for their X handle. Save it to memory (profile).
2. Make sure your box browser is signed in to that X account: have a browser subagent open https://x.com/home and report whether it's signed in and as which @handle. If it isn't, follow the sign-in skill (secure form first, then hand over the screen) so the owner can log in. Never type or guess credentials yourself.
3. Briefly explain the rule: you never block, mute, or report anyone without their explicit pick.
4. Offer to run the first sweep now. If they agree, run the X list block sweep skill.
5. Optionally offer a recurring sweep (e.g. weekly) as a routine that reports flagged lists and waits for their picks before blocking.
